'''Daniella Goldfarb''' ({{Langx|he|דניאלה גולדפרב}}) is an Israeli Israeli physical chemist at the Department of Chemical and Biological Physics at [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], where she held the Erich Klieger Professorial Chair in Chemical Physics. She joined the Institute in 1987 and is a Professor Emerita of Chemical Physics since April 2023. Her research focused on electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, methodology development and its application to structural biology and biophysics. Her scientific contributions were acknowledged by a number of international and national awards.

== Early life and education ==
Goldfarb was born in Paris.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Prof. Daniella Goldfarb {{!}} International Board 2017|url=http://www.weizmann.ac.il/conferences/InternationalBoard2017/prof-daniella-goldfarb,%20/conferences/InternationalBoard2017/prof-daniella-goldfarb|access-date=2021-06-17|website=www.weizmann.ac.il|language=en}}</ref> She studied  Chemistry at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, earning her B.Sc. degree in 1976.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=BULLETIN DU GROUPEMENT|url=https://www.ampere-society.org/bulletins/267.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190725131445/https://www.ampere-society.org/bulletins/267.pdf |archive-date=2019-07-25 }}</ref> She moved to the [[United States]] for her graduate studies for graduate studies and received an M.Sc. degree at the [[University of Rhode Island]] in 1978.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=ICE {{!}} The Israel Chemist and Engineer|url=https://ice.digitaler.co.il/ice2/75/|access-date=2021-06-17|website=ice.digitaler.co.il}}</ref> From 1979 to 1980, she worked as a research assistant at the laboratory of Clinical Toxicology at the Haim Sheeba Medical Center in Israel.

Goldfarb subsequently joined the laboratory of Prof. Zeev Luz at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where she conducted her doctoral research on the application of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques to study liquid-crystalline phases. She received her Ph.D. in 1984.<ref name=":3" /> Her doctoral research made use of [[magnetic resonance imaging]] to study liquid crystalline phases.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Goldfarb |first=Daniella |title=Magnetic resonance study of liquid crystalline phases |date=1984 |publisher=publisher not identified |location=Rehovot |language=English |oclc=884945464}}</ref> From 1984 to 1987, she carried out postdoctoral research in the laboratory of Prof. Larry Kevan at the Department of Chemistry, University of Houston, supported by a Chaim Weizmann postdoctoral fellowship from 1984 to 1986.<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
Goldfarb returned to the Weizmann Institute of Science in 1987, where she joined the Department of Isotope Research as a Scientist, initially supported by a Sir Charles Clore Fellowship (1987–1988), She was then promoted to Senior Scientist in 1988, Associate Professor in 1992 and full Professor in 1998.<ref name=":3" /> Her early research was supported by a Revson Career Development Award from 1988 to 1991. She became Professor Emerita in the Chemical and Biological Physics Department in April 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Board of Directors – קרן שוורץ רייסמן |url=https://wise.org.il/en/board-of-directors/ |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=wise.org.il}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Daniella Goldfarb |url=https://weizmann.elsevierpure.com/en/persons/daniella-goldfarb/ |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=Weizmann Institute of Science |language=en-GB}}</ref>

While an Associate Professor, Goldfarb spent a sabbatical year at Exxon Research and Engineering Company in Annandale, New Jersey from 1992 to 1993. In 1997 she held a Visiting Professorship at the Laboratory of Physical Chemistry at ETH Zurich.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Israel Chemist and Engineer |url=https://www.chemistry.org.il/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/ICE_June-2017.pdf}}</ref>

Goldfarb also took on several institutional leadership roles at the Weizmann Institute. She chaired the Chemistry Board of Studies at the Feinberg Graduate School from 1995 to 1998,<ref name=":0" /> and headed the Department of Chemical Physics from 1999 to 2003<ref name=":0" />. She served as Chair of the Council of Professors from 2009 to 2010<ref name=":4" /> and as the Institute’s President's Advisor for Advancing Women in Science from 2014 to 2018. From 2016 to 2022, she served as the Vice Chair and then Chair of the Scientific Council.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-10-18 |title=Scientific Council Chair and Vice Chair {{!}} Academic Affairs Office |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/acadaff/scientific-council/scientific-council-chair-and-vice-chair |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=www.weizmann.ac.il |language=en}}</ref>

=== Research ===
In 1987, Goldfarb returned to the Weizmann Institute of Science, where she was made a scientist in the Department of Isotope Research. She was promoted to Professor in 1998. The Goldfarb laboratory at the Weizmann Institute focused on the development and application of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy to problems in biophysics and structural biology. EPR detects the spin of unpaired electrons and provides information on the structure, dynamics, and electronic environment of paramagnetic molecules and biomolecules. Her EPR spectrometers operated primarily at high magnetic fields, specifically W-band EPR at approximately 95 GHz, which offers increased spectral resolution and sensitivity relative to standard X-band instruments.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-06-04 |title=Welcome to the Goldfarb Lab! {{!}} |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/chembiophys/EPR_group/welcome-goldfarb-lab |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=www.weizmann.ac.il |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Prof. Daniella Goldfarb - AcademiaNet|url=https://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-daniella-goldfarb/1174688|access-date=2021-06-17|website=www.academia-net.org}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=EPR Spectroscopy: Fundamentals and Methods {{!}} Wiley |url=https://www.wiley.com/en-gb/epr-spectroscopy-fundamentals-and-methods-p-9781119162995 |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=Wiley.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Gadolinium spin labeling and distance measurements ===
Among the Goldfarb group’s major contributions was the development of gadolinium(III)-based spin labels for pulse EPR distance measurements. Traditionally, distance measurements by double electron-electron resonance (DEER) relied primarily on nitroxide spin labels. However, nitroxides are readily reduced in the intracellular environment, resulting in loss of their paramagnetic signal. Gadolinium(III) complexes, in contrast, are resistant to reduction and can retain their paramagnetic properties when attached to proteins in the cellular environment. 

Beginning in 2010, Goldfarb’s group, in collaboration with the laboratory of Prof. Otting from [[Australian National University]], systematically developed the spectroscopic methodology  and a range of Gd(III)-based tags compatible with different labeling chemistries and protein types for high-field DEER distance measurements.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Potapov |first1=Alexey |last2=Yagi |first2=Hiromasa |last3=Huber |first3=Thomas |last4=Jergic |first4=Slobodan |last5=Dixon |first5=Nicholas E. |last6=Otting |first6=Gottfried |last7=Goldfarb |first7=Daniella |date=2010-07-07 |title=Nanometer-Scale Distance Measurements in Proteins Using Gd3+ Spin Labeling |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja1015662 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=132 |issue=26 |pages=9040–9048 |doi=10.1021/ja1015662 |pmid=20536233 |bibcode=2010JAChS.132.9040P |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Yagi |first1=Hiromasa |last2=Banerjee |first2=Debamalya |last3=Graham |first3=Bim |last4=Huber |first4=Thomas |last5=Goldfarb |first5=Daniella |last6=Otting |first6=Gottfried |date=2011-07-13 |title=Gadolinium Tagging for High-Precision Measurements of 6 nm Distances in Protein Assemblies by EPR |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja204415w |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=133 |issue=27 |pages=10418–10421 |doi=10.1021/ja204415w |pmid=21661728 |bibcode=2011JAChS.13310418Y |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Goldfarb |first1=Daniella |title=Gd3+ spin labeling for distance measurements by pulse EPR spectroscopy† |journal=Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics |date=2014 |volume=16 |issue=21 |pages=9685–9699 |doi=10.1039/c3cp53822b |pmid=24429839 |bibcode=2014PCCP...16.9685G |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/cp/article-abstract/16/21/9685/397320/Gd3-spin-labeling-for-distance-measurements-by|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== In-cell EPR and protein conformational dynamics ===
Goldfarb’s laboratory also developed approaches for applying EPR spectroscopy to the study of proteins within cells. Using reduction-resistant Gd(III) spin labels and high-field W-band EPR, the group established methods to deliver spin-labeled proteins into mammalian and bacterial cells and measure inter-spin distances by DEER, thereby obtaining site-specific structural information in the native cellular environment.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IES Medals and Fellows |url=https://ismar2017.org/IESawards.html |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=ismar2017.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-11-28 |title=Prof. Daniella Goldfarb on The Scientists' Channel - Weizmann Wonder Wander - News, Features and Discoveries |url=https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/chemistry/prof-daniella-goldfarb-scientists-channel |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=Weizmann Wonder Wander - News, Features and Discoveries from the Weizmann Institute of Science |language=en}}</ref> In 2016, Goldfarb was a co-author on a paper published in Nature reporting that monomeric alpha-synuclein, a protein associated with Parkinson's disease, remains intrinsically disordered within the cytosol of mammalian cells.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Theillet |first1=Francois-Xavier |last2=Binolfi |first2=Andres |last3=Bekei |first3=Beata |last4=Martorana |first4=Andrea |last5=Rose |first5=Honor May |last6=Stuiver |first6=Marchel |last7=Verzini |first7=Silvia |last8=Lorenz |first8=Dorothea |last9=van Rossum |first9=Marleen |last10=Goldfarb |first10=Daniella |last11=Selenko |first11=Philipp |date=2016-02-04 |title=Structural disorder of monomeric α-synuclein persists in mammalian cells |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature16531 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=530 |issue=7588 |pages=45–50 |doi=10.1038/nature16531 |pmid=26808899 |bibcode=2016Natur.530...45T |issn=0028-0836|hdl=11336/53199 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> The lab also extended the in-cell distance measurements  to distances between a Gd(III) spin label and a <sup>19</sup>F label on a protein residue by ENDOR (electron-nuclear double resonance).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Seal |first1=Manas |last2=Zhu |first2=Wenkai |last3=Dalaloyan |first3=Arina |last4=Feintuch |first4=Akiva |last5=Bogdanov |first5=Alexey |last6=Frydman |first6=Veronica |last7=Su |first7=Xun-Cheng |last8=Gronenborn |first8=Angela M. |last9=Goldfarb |first9=Daniella |date=2023 |title=GdIII-19F Distance Measurements for Proteins in Cells by Electron-Nuclear Double Resonance |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/anie.202218780 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |language=en |volume=62 |issue=20 |article-number=e202218780 |doi=10.1002/anie.202218780 |pmid=36905181 |bibcode=2023ACIE...62E8780S |issn=1521-3773|doi-access=free }}</ref>

=== Pulse EPR and structural biology ===
In parallel with the development of Gd(III) labels for distance measurements, the group contributed to methodological advances in pulse EPR. These included increasing sensitivity of ENDOR experiments by using echo-train detection, using shaped and chirp microwave pulses generated using arbitrary waveform generators to increase the fraction of spins excited and reduce artefacts in distance distributions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bahrenberg |first1=T. |last2=Rosenski |first2=Y. |last3=Carmieli |first3=R. |last4=Zibzener |first4=K. |last5=Qi |first5=M. |last6=Frydman |first6=V. |last7=Godt |first7=A. |last8=Goldfarb |first8=D. |last9=Feintuch |first9=A. |title=Improved sensitivity for W-band Gd(III)-Gd(III) and nitroxide-nitroxide DEER measurements with shaped pulses |journal=Journal of Magnetic Resonance (San Diego, Calif. : 1997) |date=2017 |volume=283 |pages=1–13 |doi=10.1016/j.jmr.2017.08.003 |pmid=28834777 |bibcode=2017JMagR.283....1B |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1090780717302008|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

The group applied DEER and ENDOR to a range of structural biology problems. Studies of Hsp90, an essential molecular chaperone involved in protein folding, identifying three distinct closed conformations associated with ATP, ADP and co-chaperone binding.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bruker Lectures – RSC ESR Group |url=https://www.esr-group.org/bruker-lectures/ |access-date=2026-09-20 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Giannoulis |first1=Angeliki |last2=Feintuch |first2=Akiva |last3=Barak |first3=Yoav |last4=Mazal |first4=Hisham |last5=Albeck |first5=Shira |last6=Unger |first6=Tamar |last7=Yang |first7=Feng |last8=Su |first8=Xun-Cheng |last9=Goldfarb |first9=Daniella |date=2020-01-07 |title=Two closed ATP- and ADP-dependent conformations in yeast Hsp90 chaperone detected by Mn(II) EPR spectroscopic techniques |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=117 |issue=1 |pages=395–404 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1916030116 |doi-access=free |pmid=31862713 |pmc=6955315 |bibcode=2020PNAS..117..395G |issn=0027-8424}}</ref> The group also used EPR spectroscopy to investigate molecular structure and organization within peptide/RNA coacervates and their possible relation to protein evolution.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Seal |first1=Manas |last2=Weil-Ktorza |first2=Orit |last3=Despotović |first3=Dragana |last4=Tawfik |first4=Dan S. |last5=Levy |first5=Yaakov |last6=Metanis |first6=Norman |last7=Longo |first7=Liam M. |last8=Goldfarb |first8=Daniella |date=2022-08-10 |title=Peptide-RNA Coacervates as a Cradle for the Evolution of Folded Domains |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.2c03819 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=144 |issue=31 |pages=14150–14160 |doi=10.1021/jacs.2c03819 |issn=0002-7863 |pmc=9376946 |pmid=35904499 |bibcode=2022JAChS.14414150S }}</ref>  

=== Dynamic nuclear polarization ===
Another area of Goldfarb's research concerned dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP), a technique for enhancing NMR sensitivity by transferring polarization from unpaired electron spins to nearby nuclear spins through microwave irradiation. In collaboration with the Shimon Vega's group at the Weizmann Institute, the Goldfarb group contributed to the theoretical and experimental understanding of DNP mechanisms including the cross effect and solid effect.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Shimon |first1=Daphna |last2=Hovav |first2=Yonatan |last3=Feintuch |first3=Akiva |last4=Goldfarb |first4=Daniella |last5=Vega |first5=Shimon |date=2012 |title=Dynamic nuclear polarization in the solid state: a transition between the cross effect and the solid effect |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/cp/article/14/16/5729-5743/365539 |journal=Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics |language=en |volume=14 |issue=16 |pages=5729–5743 |doi=10.1039/c2cp23915a |pmid=22419272 |bibcode=2012PCCP...14.5729S |issn=1463-9076|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |date=2015-07-15 |title=EPR Course {{!}} |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/chembiophys/EPR_group/epr-course |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=www.weizmann.ac.il |language=en}}</ref>

=== Recent research ===
Goldfarb became Professor Emerita in April 2023, and  her laboratory ceased operating as an active experimental research group in December 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-07-02 |title=News from the Goldfarb lab {{!}} |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/chembiophys/EPR_group/news-goldfarb-lab |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=www.weizmann.ac.il |language=en}}</ref> Publications arising from the group’s later research have continued to appear. methods for extending the range of distance measurements achievable by pulsed EPR spectroscopy using Gd(III) labels<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bogdanov |first1=Alexey |last2=Frydman |first2=Veronica |last3=Seal |first3=Manas |last4=Rapatskiy |first4=Leonid |last5=Schnegg |first5=Alexander |last6=Zhu |first6=Wenkai |last7=Iron |first7=Mark |last8=Gronenborn |first8=Angela M. |last9=Goldfarb |first9=Daniella |date=2024-03-06 |title=Extending the Range of Distances Accessible by 19F Electron–Nuclear Double Resonance in Proteins Using High-Spin Gd(III) Labels |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.3c13745 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=146 |issue=9 |pages=6157–6167 |doi=10.1021/jacs.3c13745 |issn=0002-7863 |pmc=10921402 |pmid=38393979 |bibcode=2024JAChS.146.6157B }}</ref>; determination of the zero-field splitting axes of Gd(III)-complexes  for spin-label structural analysis<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bogdanov |first1=Alexey |last2=Frydman |first2=Veronica |last3=Su |first3=Xun-Cheng |last4=Seal |first4=Manas |last5=Zhu |first5=Wenkai |last6=Gronenborn |first6=Angela M. |last7=Schnegg |first7=Alexander |last8=Goldfarb |first8=Daniella |date=2026-06-17 |title=Unlocking Gd(III) Anisotropy: Determining the Zero-Field Splitting Axes to Enhance Spin-Label Structural Analysis |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c22555 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=148 |issue=23 |pages=23597–23610 |doi=10.1021/jacs.5c22555 |issn=0002-7863 |pmc=13281530 |pmid=42227957 |bibcode=2026JAChS.14823597B }}</ref>; structural studies into the disordered C-terminal tail of Hsp90.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Edinach |first1=Elena |last2=Giannouli |first2=Angeliki |last3=Dalaloyan |first3=Arina |last4=Oranges |first4=Maria |last5=Banik |first5=Debasis |last6=Yardeni |first6=Elian Hadas |last7=Elimelech |first7=Annika |last8=Sattler |first8=Michael |last9=Ntermanakis |first9=Emmanouil |last10=Su |first10=Xun-Cheng |last11=Goldfarb |first11=Daniella |date=2026-04-22 |title=Beyond a Passive Tether: Structural Insights into the Disordered Tail of Hsp90 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=148 |issue=15 |pages=16469–16481 |doi=10.1021/jacs.6c04189 |issn=1520-5126 |pmc=13107436 |pmid=41954606 |bibcode=2026JAChS.14816469E }}</ref> 

=== Influence and recognition ===
Goldfarb’s work on Gd(III)-based spin labeling contributed to the development of EPR methods for obtaining structural information on proteins within cells, including measurements of inter-spin distances in the cellular environment.

Her textbook, ''EPR Spectroscopy: Fundamentals and Methods'', co-edited with Stefan Stoll of the University of Washington, and published by Wiley in 2018, is the first volume devoted to electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy in the eMagRes Handbook series.<ref name=":5" />

=== Lectures and teaching ===
In 2014, Goldfarb recorded a six-part introductory lecture series on EPR spectroscopy for the Australia and New Zealand Society for Magnetic Resonance (ANZMAG). The series covers topics from basic principles of EPR to pulse double-resonance techniques; the series remains publicly available online.<ref name=":6" /> In 2026, she delivered  a tutorial lecture on EPR at the EUROMAR conference in Goteborg Sweden. 

=== Editorial and service roles ===
Goldfarb held several leadership positions in the international magnetic resonance community. She served as President of the European Federation of EPR Groups from 2000 to 2003,<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=efepr |url=https://efepr.org/About.html |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=efepr.org}}</ref> and as Vice President of Groupment AMPERE (Europe) from 2002 to 2010. She was Vice President of the International Society of Magnetic Resonance (ISMAR) from 2011 to 2013 and President from 2014 to 2017. Goldfarb also held a number of editorial and advisory board positions. She served on the advisory board of Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics from 2007 to 2011 and again from 2015, and chaired its editorial board from 2012 to 2014. She was executive editor of Magnetic Resonance from 2019 to 2025<ref>{{Cite web |title=MR - Editorial board |url=https://www.magnetic-resonance-ampere.net/editorial_board.html |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=www.magnetic-resonance-ampere.net}}</ref> and served on the editorial board of the Journal of Magnetic Resonance from 2003 to 2023.
